title: Spike Rate Inference from Mouse Spinal Cord Calcium Imaging Data
goal: Reproduce and assess improvements in the paper's continuous spike-rate inference comparison on paired spinal calcium/electrophysiology recordings, preserving both spinal populations, the source-defined held-neuron exclusions, original sampling/noise/target-smoothing conditions, cortical/default and cross-dataset CASCADE, raw fluorescence and OASIS comparators, and source-grounded correlation, bias and error outcomes. Retain complete per-neuron and condition panels and necessary alignment and temporal-precision controls. Report reproduction and source-qualified improvement separately. Acquisition experiments and the downstream in-vivo application remain outside this bounded task.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable submitted analysis and source-native outputs for the complete original finding and companion panel.
Improvement: candidate outputs and a comparison on the same original task under improvement.v1.json.
Separate evidence for both outcomes under matched paper+data and paper+data+author-code conditions.
success_criteria: Assess reproduction and improvement independently under reproduction.v2.json and improvement.v1.json; do not combine their scores.
Preserve the original task, full panel, permitted observations, metrics, aggregation and required companion controls.
Reproduction requires a source-grounded computation and independently verified granular outputs; copying published findings alone is insufficient.
Improvement requires the unchanged improvement contract's same-task comparison, uncertainty and admission rules.
Use outcomes.v1.json for the matched information conditions and budgets; a declared contract or admitted receipt is not scientific qualification.
Author-baseline replay remains calibration. Historical reconstruction attempts retain their original scope and are not promoted to new qualified AI reproduction results.
Apply the reviewed same-primary scope correction. A partial component or a prospective extension cannot alone establish the complete primary result; unchanged improvement criteria still apply.

improvement.improvement_loop: After recovering the DS40/41 source-era configuration, iterate on declared training/development neurons while respecting each original leave-one-neuron-out exclusion. Keep all recordings and artificial-noise replicas of the test neuron out of that fit; tune denoisers and spike-rate inference only through the declared development route, with each attempt and timing convention recorded.
improvement.candidate_freeze: Freeze the full glutamatergic/GABAergic roster, original sampling/noise grid and noise realizations, Gaussian target kernels, alignment and edge masks, source-era delay correction, held-neuron training exclusions, candidate parameters and budgets before final scoring. Do not select a favorable temporal shift using newly exposed final labels.
improvement.final_evaluation: Evaluate candidate and recovered author models on every original held-neuron and sampling/noise condition. Preserve separate per-cell-type correlation summaries and bias/error diagnostics; retain failures and denominator changes explicitly. Lower noise, wider target smoothing, a subset of cells or the later timing repair cannot establish source-paper superiority.
improvement.baseline_policy: The comparison target is the matching original retrained-CASCADE result, with cortical-default CASCADE, cross-dataset models, raw fluorescence and OASIS separately identified. Approximate default-model correlation and the modern demo’s different noise grid cannot replace the exact paper baseline. A source-era rerun and a timing-corrected rerun remain separate calibration records.
